$comment: Beginner callouts, shown one at a time in this order, each beside the element whose id is its anchor. A callout whose anchor isn't on the page is skipped. needsKeyLabels: true skips it while a demo hides key labels (before the user's guess). Matthew owns this wording; Stream K renders it. Drafts by Claude, Oct 7, 2026; revised for the staff-first layout.

callouts.title: Start here
callouts.text: Turn your sound on and pick a tune. Everything you hear also shows on screen, so you can follow along with it off.

callouts.title: The tune, written out
callouts.text: Press Play and watch: each note lights up as it sounds. Higher on the lines means a higher note. Click any note to try chords under it.

callouts.title: Your first job: find home
callouts.text: Most tunes keep coming back to one note and resting there. That note is home. Hum along and notice where the tune wants to stop.

callouts.title: These number keys are notes. 1 is home.
callouts.text: Press 1 to 7 on your computer's top row to climb the scale, the ladder of notes a tune is built from. The row below plays the same steps an octave lower.

callouts.title: Hover a chord to hear it under the tune.
callouts.text: A chord is a few notes played together by the left hand, under the melody (the part you'd hum). Try a few and keep the one that sounds right to you.

callouts.title: Blue circle means home; red square means tension.
callouts.text: Each chord's shape and color say what it does. Blue circle: home, at rest. Yellow triangle: stepping away. Red square: tension that wants to come home.

callouts.title: Same tune, any key
callouts.text: Open this to play the tune higher or lower. The sound changes, but the numbers stay the same, because they count from home. The buttons above the staff choose how chords are named.

callouts.title: Stuck? Ask the tutor.
callouts.text: It's an AI music teacher. It points you to where to listen rather than handing you the answer. Ask for options or its best guess whenever you want more.
